subject: art-design
title: Printmaking Methods: Foundations
welcome_lead: Meet the four print families and what makes each one tick.
meta_desc: GCSE printmaking foundations: relief, intaglio, planographic and stencil methods.
final_note: Each family solves the same problem differently.

concepts.def: Ink sits on raised areas of a cut block.
Ink sits in recessed lines cut into a plate.
Print made from a flat surface like stone.
A set of identical prints from one block.
Aligning multiple layers exactly on paper.

walkthroughs.body_html: In relief, you cut away the bits you do not want to print. Ink covers what is left standing — a lino block, a woodcut or a stamp. Pressed onto paper, the raised areas leave a positive mark.

Intaglio works the other way. Lines are scratched or etched into a metal plate, ink is rubbed into the grooves and wiped off the surface. A heavy press squeezes paper into the lines to lift the ink. Drypoint and etching are intaglio.

Planographic processes like lithography print from a flat surface using the fact that oil and water repel. Stencil prints, like screen-print, push ink through gaps in a mesh. Across all four families, an edition is a numbered run.
